title: SYSK Selects: How Acne Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun episode on acne. Josh introduces the episode, then the hosts cover skin anatomy (epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous layer, sebum, hair follicles and sebaceous glands), how clogged pores lead to comedones, whiteheads and blackheads, pustules, papules, nodules, cysts, milia, pre-pubertal acne, rosacea, myths about diet, makeup, and genetics, treatments (benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, antibiotics, chemical peels, birth control pills, lasers, extraction), and a Type S/Type L serotonin transporter personality digression. The episode closes with listener mail from Tyler Davis about the show and a correction on fail-safe design and the buttered-toast myth, plus plugs for the Super Stuff Guide to Happiness audiobook and social media.

segments.title: Josh's introduction to the Selects episode
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects episode on acne, noting it is gross but fascinating, then the hosts open with banter.

segments.title: Skin facts and structure
segments.summary: The hosts discuss skin facts from a prior skincare writing project: lip skin layers, shower temperature, the skin as the largest organ (about ten pounds), and the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous layers.

segments.title: Skin cell turnover, sebum and hair follicles
segments.summary: New skin cells form in lower layers and move outward over about a month, with roughly forty to sixty million cells shed per day. Dead cells mix with sebum and lipids to form a waterproof, bacteria-resisting barrier. Hair follicles connect to sebaceous glands that release oil.

segments.title: How clogged pores cause acne
segments.summary: Acne forms when too many dead skin cells and excess sebum block pores and follicles. Puberty raises sebum production. Bacteria, specifically Propionibacterium acnes, feed on sebum and trigger inflammation.

segments.title: Whiteheads, blackheads, pustules, papules and nodules
segments.summary: The hosts explain open and closed comedones, the Latin origin of the word comedo, why blackheads are dark (oxidized, not dirt), and how whiteheads can become pustules. They also cover papules, nodules, and cysts, with the American Academy of Dermatology's definitions described as confusing.

segments.title: Milia, pre-pubertal acne and rosacea
segments.summary: Milia are small white bumps common in newborns that usually clear on their own, and can occasionally occur in adults. Pre-pubertal acne in young children is linked to early androgen production and warrants a doctor visit. Rosacea involves flushing and bumps on the nose, and is sometimes confused with gin blossoms.

segments.title: Myths and causes: diet, makeup, genetics, dirt
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether diet, genetics, dirt, and makeup cause acne. Doctors mostly call the greasy-food link a myth, though insulin effects and omega-3 and iodide in shellfish may matter. Genetics has an effect but is overestimated. Dirt on the surface does not cause acne. Non-comedogenic makeup and sleeping in makeup are discussed.

segments.title: Acne treatments
segments.summary: Benzoyl peroxide kills P. acnes and dries skin, while salicylic acid clears pores. Gentle washing, avoiding over-washing and harsh scrubbing, moisturizing, showering after exercise, and loose clothing are advised. Antibiotics, chemical peels, birth control pills, lasers, and professional extraction are discussed.

segments.title: Personality, stress and the serotonin transporter gene
segments.summary: The hosts briefly discuss stress and the advice to be more relaxed. They describe a blog-post explanation linking a serotonin transporter gene variant (the L and S alleles) to personality, and compare it to Type A and Type B personalities.
